## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly grounds the 2011 minimality conjecture, but supplies no theorem-level evidence about the 2024 result.
- claim-2: Correctly preserves the stronger integral indecomposables statement as distinct from minimality. Nothing supplied shows that the 2024 theorem proves torsion-freeness or the displayed free-abelian isomorphism.
- claim-3: Automatic DOI/provider escalation was executed, but produced only metadata and an abstract. “We prove the minimality conjecture” does not identify the exact coefficient ring, hypotheses, ideals, generating families, or theorem conclusion. It therefore cannot establish applicability to the current \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\).

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] After retrieving the theorem text, provide a line-by-line correspondence between its coefficient ring, parameters, \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), and generating families and those of the 2011 conjecture; separately record whether it proves only minimality or also the stated indecomposables isomorphism.
- [computation] For the retrieved primary-source artifact, record its SHA-256 digest and machine-checkable page/line or byte-range mappings for every quoted theorem and definition passage.
- [source-refresh] Starting from DOI `10.1112/jlms.12832` or exact matching arXiv metadata, ingest bounded numbered primary-source passages containing the relevant definitions, coefficient ring, parameter hypotheses, both generating families, numbered minimality theorem, and any statement concerning \(J/\Lambda_+J\), with stable locators.

## Required revisions
- State that metadata escalation succeeded but theorem-text retrieval and independent review did not.
- **Requested target established: no.** Minimality is not theorem-level established from the supplied evidence, and the stronger indecomposables claim remains separately unestablished.
- Do not substitute the abstract-level announcement or the stronger parent claim for the exact 2024 theorem.
